name: FT2232HL-REEL
title: FT2232H: dual high-speed USB 2.0 to UART / FIFO / MPSSE bridge, LQFP-64 and QFN-64
summary: A USB 2.0 high-speed (480 Mb/s) device with two independent ports, each configurable as a UART up to 12 Mbaud, a 245-style parallel FIFO, a bit-bang port or an MPSSE engine for JTAG, SPI and I2C; channel A alone can run a 60 MHz synchronous FIFO, and the chip also offers host bus emulation, a CPU-style FIFO and an opto-isolated fast serial link. It runs from 3.3 V with an on-chip 1.8 V regulator for the core, needs a 12 MHz crystal, and takes its mode and USB descriptors from an optional 93C46/56/66 EEPROM. I/O is 5 V tolerant; operating range -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 2.0 high speed 480 Mb/s, full speed 12 Mb/s
2 independent, 4 kbyte TX and RX buffer each
VCCIO 2.97 V to 3.63 V; VCORE 1.62 V to 1.98 V; VPHY/VPLL 3.0 V to 3.6 V
70 mA typ; 500 µA typ in suspend
30 mA typ, 60 mA max at 480 MHz
±2 kV HBM, ±200 V MM, ±500 V CDM

circuits.title: USB to RS232, channel A
circuits.description: Bus-powered FT2232H with channel A as a full RS232 port. VBUS feeds a 3.3 V regulator (U3) that supplies VCCIO, VREGIN and, through ferrite beads L1 and L2 with 4.7 µF and 100 nF each, VPLL and VPHY. The on-chip regulator's 1.8 V output carries 3.3 µF and runs the VCORE pins. A 93C46 EEPROM holds the configuration, a 12 MHz crystal with two 27 pF caps sets the clock, 12 kΩ sets REF and 1 kΩ holds RESET# high. ADBUS0 to ADBUS7 carry the eight TTL modem lines to a MAX3241 (three drivers, five receivers) whose charge pump uses five 100 nF caps; PWREN# drives its receiver enable and SUSPEND# its shutdown, so the transceiver idles while the USB link sleeps. ACBUS3 and ACBUS4 sink current through two LEDs with 220 Ω resistors to show receive and transmit traffic. Channel B can carry a second copy of the same port.
notes: J1 pins: VBUS 1, D- 2, D+ 3, GND 4; SHIELD is the connector shell. Y1 pins 1 and 2 are the crystal's pins 1 and 3. U2 pins: CS 1, SCL 2, D 3, Q 4, GND 5, ORG 6, DU 7, VCC 8.

U4 pins: C2+ 1, C2- 2, V- 3, R1IN to R5IN 4 to 8, T1OUT to T3OUT 9 to 11, T3IN 12, T2IN 13, T1IN 14, R5OUT to R1OUT 15 to 19, R2OUTB 20, R1OUTB 21, SHDN 22, EN 23, C1- 24, GND 25, VCC 26, V+ 27, C1+ 28. J2 is a DB9 with its shell pins 10 and 11 open.

circuits.title: Dual RS422
circuits.description: Both channels run as TTL-level UARTs. Each channel uses two full-duplex transceivers: one carries TXD and RXD, the other RTS# and CTS#, each pair as a differential line on a DB9-M. Every receiver input pair has a 120 Ω terminator. SUSPEND# enables all drivers and PWREN# (active low) enables all receivers, so the transceivers drop to low quiescent current during USB suspend. DTR#, DSR#, DCD# and RI# are unused.
notes: Transceiver pin numbers on the RTS#/CTS# device: RO 2, RE# 3, DE 4, DI 5, ground 6 and 7.
VCC is the transceiver supply.

circuits.title: Dual RS485
circuits.description: Both channels run as TTL-level UARTs into half-duplex RS485 transceivers on a two-wire bus, one DB9-M per channel. Each channel's TXDEN pin switches its driver on only while a character is going out; PWREN# drives the active-low receiver enables, turning the receivers off in USB suspend. A 120 Ω resistor in series with a link across each pair terminates the cable when the board sits at one of its ends. The transmitting node also receives its own data; ORing the receiver output with TXDEN in a gate such as an HC32 before RXD removes that echo in hardware.

circuits.title: Fast opto-isolated serial interface
circuits.description: Channel B's four fast-serial lines cross an isolation barrier through two HCPL-2430 dual opto-couplers. VCC5V is the USB VBUS supply and VCCE the external device's supply. Each photodiode LED is fed from the supply of the side that drives it, with 470 Ω in the driving line; each open-collector output has a 1 kΩ pull-up to its own side's supply. FSDI and FSCLK come in through U2; FSDO and FSCTS go out through U3 to the external DO and CTS lines.

circuits.title: USB bus powered
circuits.description: The board takes all its power from VBUS. A 3.3 V regulator feeds VCCIO, VREGIN and, through a ferrite bead and 4.7 µF plus 100 nF each, VPLL and VPHY. The on-chip regulator's 1.8 V output, with at least 3.3 µF, supplies VCORE. Each VCORE and VCCIO pin has 100 nF. A 93C46 EEPROM with 10 kΩ pull-ups on CS, clock and data out and 2.2 kΩ between EEDATA and the data output holds the configuration; a 12 MHz crystal with 27 pF caps, 12 kΩ on REF, 1 kΩ on RESET# and TEST to ground complete it. The USB shell goes to ground through 0 Ω.
notes: J1 pins: VBUS 1, D- 2, D+ 3, GND 4; SHIELD is the connector shell. Y1 pins 1 and 2 are the crystal's pins 1 and 3. U2 pins: CS 1, SCL 2, D 3, Q 4, GND 5, ORG 6, DU 7, VCC 8.

circuits.title: USB bus powered, separate 1.8 V regulator
circuits.description: Like the plain bus-powered design, but a second regulator makes 1.8 V for VCORE from VBUS. The on-chip regulator is not used: VREGIN and VREGOUT stay open and the 3.3 µF goes.
notes: J1 pins: VBUS 1, D- 2, D+ 3, GND 4; SHIELD is the connector shell. Y1 pins 1 and 2 are the crystal's pins 1 and 3. U2 pins: CS 1, SCL 2, D 3, Q 4, GND 5, ORG 6, DU 7, VCC 8.

circuits.title: USB self powered
circuits.description: An external supply, through a 3.3 V regulator, powers the chip; USB supplies no current. VBUS only reaches BCBUS7 through a 4.7 kΩ / 10 kΩ divider, so the pin works as PWRSAV# and holds the chip in suspend while no powered host is attached. The EEPROM is set for self-powered operation with suspend on BCBUS7 low, which rules out MPSSE on channel B. Otherwise as the bus-powered design.
notes: J1 pins: VBUS 1, D- 2, D+ 3, GND 4; SHIELD is the connector shell. Y1 pins 1 and 2 are the crystal's pins 1 and 3. U2 pins: CS 1, SCL 2, D 3, Q 4, GND 5, ORG 6, DU 7, VCC 8.
J2 pin 1 is the external supply, pin 2 its ground.

circuits.title: USB self powered, separate 1.8 V regulator
circuits.description: Self powered, with both 3.3 V and 1.8 V made by regulators from the external supply; VREGIN and VREGOUT stay open. The VBUS divider on BCBUS7 and the EEPROM settings are as in the self-powered design.
notes: J1 pins: VBUS 1, D- 2, D+ 3, GND 4; SHIELD is the connector shell. Y1 pins 1 and 2 are the crystal's pins 1 and 3. U2 pins: CS 1, SCL 2, D 3, Q 4, GND 5, ORG 6, DU 7, VCC 8.
J2 pin 1 is the external supply, pin 2 its ground.

circuits.title: 12 MHz crystal oscillator
circuits.description: A 12 MHz parallel-cut crystal (±0.003 %) across OSCI and OSCO with a load capacitor from each pin to ground. 27 pF suits many crystals; where the crystal's manufacturer recommends a load value, use that. A 12 MHz oscillator with CMOS output may drive OSCI instead, with OSCO left open.

operation.text: Two independent interfaces sit behind one USB 2.0 high-speed (480 Mb/s) device. Each can be a UART, a 245-style FIFO, JTAG, SPI, I2C or bit-bang port with its own baud rate generator; the chip also offers host bus emulation, a CPU-style FIFO and a fast opto-isolated serial link. The USB protocol is handled entirely on chip, with no firmware to write.
Each interface has a 4 kbyte transmit buffer (host to chip) and a 4 kbyte receive buffer (chip to host), managed by the USB protocol engine.

UART (RS232, RS422, RS485) to 12 Mbaud; 7, 9, 10 and 11 Mbaud are not supported. The baud rate is programmable from 183 baud to 12 Mbaud. Parallel FIFO up to 8 Mbyte/s; synchronous parallel FIFO above 25 Mbyte/s, and single-channel synchronous FIFO up to 40 Mbyte/s. MPSSE sustains up to 30 Mbit/s.
Each UART gets a x16 or x10 clock derived from a 120 MHz reference by a 14-bit prescaler plus 4 bits that add a fractional part to the divisor.
A driver timeout flushes short packets back to the host. Default 16 ms, settable 0 to 255 ms; at 0 ms a packet goes on every high-speed microframe.

7 or 8 data bits, 1 or 2 stop bits, odd, even, mark, space or no parity. Hardware RTS/CTS and DTR/DSR handshaking or X-On/X-Off; full modem lines; TXDEN for RS485 driver enable; TX and RX LED outputs per channel.

An on-chip LDO makes 1.8 V for the core and the USB transceiver from a 3.3 V VREGIN; a filter capacitor on VREGIN is recommended. VREGOUT has no internal path to the core: the board must wire VREGOUT to the VCORE pins.

The UTMI PHY handles high-speed and full-speed serialisation, SYNC/EOP, clock recovery, bit stuffing and resume/suspend signalling, and its PLL makes the chip's clocks from a 12 MHz crystal on OSCI/OSCO. REF needs 12 kΩ to GND. VPHY must come from a 3.3 V regulator rather than straight from VBUS; an LC filter is recommended on both VPHY and VPLL.
An internal power-on reset starts the chip. RESET# lets an outside device reset it; tie RESET# to VCCIO when unused.

Without an EEPROM, or with a blank one, both channels come up as asynchronous serial ports using VID 0403, PID 6010, the built-in product description and power descriptor, and no serial number. A 93C46, 93C56 or 93C66 (16-bit wide, 1 Mbit/s clock at 3.0 V to 3.6 V, for example 93LC46B) sets each channel's mode (UART, 245 FIFO, CPU FIFO, fast serial), the VID, PID, serial number, strings, power descriptor, remote wake-up, pull-down in suspend and I/O drive strength. It is programmed in circuit over USB with FTDI's MPROG (V3.4a or later), so a blank part can be fitted and programmed at test.

After reset each channel takes the mode stored in the EEPROM. Once enumerated, the application sends FT_SetBitMode through the driver to put a channel in MPSSE or in one of the two bit-bang modes (async or sync). Set Bit Mode values: 0x0 reset, 0x1 async bit-bang, 0x2 MPSSE, 0x4 sync bit-bang, 0x8 host bus emulation, 0x40 synchronous FIFO.

Channel A only. Both channels must first be set to asynchronous 245 FIFO in the EEPROM; software then selects synchronous FIFO, and channel A takes over channel B's buffers, leaving channel B unavailable. The chip outputs a 60 MHz CLKOUT and data moves on its rising edge; only a read or a write happens at a time. Channel B pins stay as they were when async FIFO was chosen: if never used, D7:0 float high through 75 kΩ, TXE# is low, RXF# high, and RD# and WR# are inputs that should be pulled high. An MPSSE set_data_bits command can first make channel B all inputs.

The chip drops RXF# when data is waiting. The system takes OE# low to turn the bus round (at least one clock before RD#), then RD# low; the first byte is on the bus once OE# is low and a new byte follows each clock RD# is sampled low. Wait states are made by lifting RD#. RXF# goes high when the buffer is empty; bus data after that is invalid.
With TXE# low, the system puts data on the bus and takes WR# low; a byte is taken every clock in which both TXE# and WR# are low, so bursts run while TXE# stays low.

Channels A and B. Like the synchronous FIFO but without CLKOUT or OE#: a byte is read on RD# falling (next byte fetched on RD# rising, RXF# then going high until another byte waits) and written on WR# falling. RXF# and TXE# float with a 200 kΩ pull-up to VCCIO during reset.

Each channel has a multi-protocol synchronous serial engine for JTAG, SPI, I2C or a custom synchronous protocol, or for loading SRAM FPGAs over USB. It is driven by commands embedded in the data stream, singly or in packets. CLKOUT is 30 MHz at most and can be divided down. One channel can be MPSSE while the other is a UART or 245 FIFO, or both can be MPSSE.

An MPSSE option, off by default: after asserting TCK the chip waits for the target to return the clock on GPIOL3 (RTCK, as used by ARM cores) before changing its data output, which changes on the falling edge of TCK.

Both channels together emulate an 8048/8051 bus: AD7..AD0 multiplexed address/data, A15..A8 upper address, CS#, ALE, RD#, WR#, IORDY, CLKOUT and two MPSSE-controlled lines I/O0 and I/O1. Four operations: read, extended read, write, extended write (the extended ones change A15..A8). CLKOUT is always 60 MHz in this mode; the clock divisor has no effect. With Div By 5 on, a read returns 2 bytes, otherwise 1; at a 16.67 ns clock most peripherals need Div By 5. Holding IORDY low stretches every cycle; tie it up to VCORE when unused. I/O1 can make the chip wait for a level, so it can serve as a peripheral's interrupt input; it must stay an input for that.

An SJA1000 CAN controller connects directly: CS#, ALE (to ALE/AS), RD#, WR# and AD[7:0] in parallel, I/O1 to the controller's INT#, IORDY and the controller's MODE pin each tied to Vcc, and the controller's Tx/Rx to a CAN transceiver and the bus.

A synchronous four-wire link (FSDI, FSCLK, FSDO, FSCTS) on channel B that tolerates opto-isolators in its path. The external side supplies FSCLK and so sets the rate in both directions; full-speed USB rates are reachable. An address bit in each frame picks channel A or B, so both channels can share the four wires. Enabled in the EEPROM; a Set Bit Bang Mode value of 10 holds it in reset (data is accepted but not sent) and 0x0 releases it.

Outgoing: when it has data and is not receiving, the chip sends a 0 start bit on FSDO, eight data bits LSB first, then a source bit (0 = channel A, 1 = channel B), clocked by the external FSCLK; a receiver that is not ready stops FSCLK. Incoming: the external device may start when FSCTS is high, sending a 0 start bit, eight bits LSB first and a destination bit (0 = A, 1 = B; data goes to the other channel if the named one is not in fast serial mode). FSCTS falls on the clock after the start bit and remains low while the chip is not ready for another byte.

Either channel, set in the EEPROM. CS# and A0 select the data pipe (A0 = 0) or status/send-immediate (A0 = 1) for RD# and WR#. A microcontroller can drive D0..D7, RD#, WR#, A0 and CS# from its ports, optionally also SIWU and PWREN#.

Either channel's eight lines become a parallel port, each pin set as input or output by a mask in the SETUP command. Asynchronous mode clocks written data out at the baud-rate generator's pace and brings RDSTB#/WRSTB# out for external logic; pins hold the last value until new data arrives. Synchronous mode only touches the pins when the host writes, reading the inputs just before driving the new output, so data read back lags one byte behind (send 0x55, 0xAA from 0xFF and read 0xFF, 0x55). To read pins that are all inputs, bytes must still be written.

SIWU# works in FIFO and bit-bang modes. With the bus awake (PWREN# = 0) a 250 ns low pulse sends whatever is in the transmit buffer on the next bulk-IN request without waiting for the latency timer, flagged by the falling edge; use it only after writes to the chip stop. In suspend (PWREN# = 1) with remote wake-up enabled, a 20 ms low pulse asks the host to resume. Tie SIWU to VCCIO when unused. RI# does the same wake-up job in UART mode.

With remote wake-up enabled the peripheral may draw up to 2.5 mA in suspend, otherwise 500 µA. Pull-ups should stay powered in suspend and no path may half-power the peripheral. With the pull-down option enabled the chip will not wake from suspend.
In UART mode TXLED# and RXLED# per channel go from high impedance to low on transfers, stretched by a digital one-shot. LEDs connect to the VCCIO supply.

I/O pins are 3.3 V cells that tolerate 5 V; the USB PHY pins do not. Drive strength (4, 8, 12 or 16 mA) and slew rate are EEPROM settings. Unused pins marked ** default to inputs with about 75 kΩ to VCCIO.

Passes USB 2.0 compliance with USB-IF test ID 40720019. Edge rates depend on layout, external parts and protection on the data lines; they can be trimmed by an EEPROM setting or by passives on the USB lines.

Bus powered: VBUS through a 3.3 V regulator supplies VCCIO, VPLL, VPHY and VREGIN; VCORE comes from VREGOUT (at least 3.3 µF) or from a separate 1.8 V regulator. Self powered: an external supply does the same and VBUS only signals attachment on BCBUS7 (PWRSAV#). VPHY may not be fed from VBUS directly.

The QFN's pin 1 marking (dot, chamfer or both) is tied inside to the 4.35 x 4.35 mm centre pad on the underside, not to the die ground. It may be connected to system ground but should not serve as the device's ground point. Corner leads may be chamfered.
MSL 3: 168 hours floor life out of the bag at 30 °C / 60 % RH; beyond that, bake at +125 °C for up to 17 hours.
Free virtual COM port (VCP) and D2XX drivers present the device as a serial port or a DLL-level device on Windows, Mac OS X and Linux.
